parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a tier-1 universal document exposure with tier-1/tier-2 facility and custody exposures, partially offset by courts that demonstrably grant relief. Every trans visitor carries an inescapable entry/document exposure: X markers and self-selection abolished, markers fixed to sex assigned at birth, Supreme Court-allowed restrictions, consular cable ordering refusal where sex is in doubt, and a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report confiscated passports and stranding, and eight-plus governments issued advisories. Facility bans reach government buildings and, in the division, schools and colleges since May 2026, with one documented trespass arrest and 24-hour men's-ward holding. If detained, immigration custody documents beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; federal corrections impose hormone-removal 'conversion' policies. Offsetting this: no criminalisation of trans identity itself, no death-penalty pathway, working courts enjoining orders and denying a stay, a federal hate-crime statute and employment protection, active litigation and legal aid. Public opinion is majority-hostile on documents (66%) and sports (69%). Severity sits above the 0.35 exclusion anchors, roughly at the 0.45 universal-friction anchors, well below criminalisation tiers.

entry_documents.exposure: Executive order redefining binary sex; X markers and self-selection ended; markers only M/F per supporting documents; Supreme Court allowed restrictions (Nov 2025). Consular cable directs refusal on 'reasonable doubt' of sex and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility. Travellers report passports confiscated or blocked and being stranded abroad; eight-plus foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; pending civil-liberties litigation; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch → refusal/possible fraud finding → immigration custody, where documented abuse against trans detainees applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Transgender men in immigration custody reported forced-labour programmes, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse, with guards invoking their gender. Federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cut short, hormones removed, psychiatric substitution). A trans woman arrested under a bathroom law was held 24 hours in a men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders blocked or enjoined; federal hate-crime statute; active civil litigation; courts denying stays in at least one challenge.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or document discrepancy escalates into custody where birth-sex placement and treatment restrictions operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities. Maps show bans in 9+1 states covering all government buildings, 9 more covering schools and some buildings, 3 schools-only, and 6 extending to private settings; 4 states make use criminal in certain circumstances. The division extended its 2024 ban to public colleges and universities on 15 May 2026. A trans student was arrested and handcuffed at a capitol restroom (Mar 2025).
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states plus capital district have no mapped ban; a national appellate order plus Supreme Court denial of stay blocks enforcement against one student plaintiff during litigation; trespass offence requires refusal to depart.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility rule plus trespass charge → arrest → men's-ward holding; schools ban reaches a travelling family's minor directly.

care_services.exposure: Executive order frames gender-affirming care for minors as 'mutilation'; youth care banned in 27 states; October 2025 proposed rule would bar public insurance reimbursement under 18; specialised LGBTQ youth lifeline shut; DOJ subpoenaed paediatric patient records. A parent travelling with a trans minor faces care denial and possible state inquiry.
care_services.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined in court; no documented refusal of emergency adult care.
care_services.interaction: Family travel intersects minors' care bans, school facility rules and record-subpoena exposure simultaneously.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: December 2025 DOJ reward memorandum uses 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist framing; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups 'radically pro-transgender'; January 2025 order directs law enforcement to investigate schools and potentially prosecute teachers; forbidden-terms lists and removed LGBTQ webpages; advocates compare the posture to early genocide stages.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The memorandum states the reward is not conditioned on that phrase; the strategy says counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; employment and hate-crime protections remain in force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the severity attached to any outing that brings a traveller to police attention.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division ban requires students in public schools, colleges and universities to use birth-sex restrooms; national order threatens criminal investigation and prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; sports bans (division 2022, national 2025); youth care bans in 27 states. For a visiting parent these can force care denial, exclusion from school or camp programmes, or state inquiry.
minors_guardians.protection: Litigation pending; the order is blocked or enjoined in part; a district court struck a related school-discussion statute; enforcement against one plaintiff is suspended.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family encounters school facility rules, care restrictions and official inquiry risk at once.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented restroom arrest with handcuffing and men's-ward holding; 2025 polling shows 66% backing sex-at-birth document rules and 69% backing sex-based sports rules; the division has no hate-crime statute and its sodomy provision is unrepealed (secondary); travel advisories from allied governments signal perceived risk. No trans-specific violence rate or denominator is provided.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; federal employment non-discrimination ruling; no national sodomy law; national crime data show bias incidents are a small minority of reported crime.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Majority-hostile opinion plus division-level absence of bias coverage weakens recourse for street incidents, while federal coverage partially compensates.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport challenge, executive-order challenges and the 2025 health rules all unresolved, so exposure at travel date is uncertain; enforcement varies by state and officer; division law's scope unsettled pending merits; no current trans-specific violence statistics; corrections bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner counts from 2025.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Multiple injunctions and a Supreme Court denial of stay show courts working for trans litigants; legal-aid FAQ, equality maps and running trackers; 22 states plus capital district bar gender-identity discrimination.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty cuts both ways: measures may be enjoined by travel date, but facility and document rules are presently operative where mapped.

anchor_checks.comparison: Varnalia criminalises presentation, holds visitors months in beating-prone pretrial custody with a live capital clause and courts deferring to security services. This jurisdiction criminalises no trans status or expression as such, has no death-penalty pathway for gender identity, and its courts actively enjoin hostile measures. Custody abuse exists but is subset-specific, not the routine entry outcome. Clearly above 0.15.

Vesskar's routine verification exposure at checkpoints, documented detention, humiliation and denial of care, narrow anti-discrimination claims, scarce legal aid and inconsistent enforcement closely parallel this dossier's document and facility regime. This jurisdiction adds documented immigration-custody abuse and one criminal restroom arrest (worse), but also a federal hate-crime statute, sustained injunctions and Supreme Court relief for a plaintiff (better). Rough parity.

Meridia accepts markers matching presentation with trained, respectful border officers, brief detention ending in release, written reasons, counsel and compensation. This jurisdiction does the opposite at entry: markers abolished for mismatch, refusal directed on sex doubt, possible lifetime bar, stranded travellers. It sits far below 0.75 on entry exposure despite comparable-or-better court functionality.

Ostravia mandates birth-sex prison housing with frequent assault, criminalises cross-dressing in official buildings, and offers only slow, uncertain remedies. This dossier's custody harms (immigration abuse, hormone removal) are severe but reach only those entering custody, while cross-dressing is not criminalised and remedies demonstrably succeed in court. Sits above 0.25.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces an inescapable document exposure at entry — markers abolished, refusal directed on sex doubt, possible lifetime ineligibility, documented confiscation and stranding — layered with facility bans reaching government buildings and, in this division, schools and colleges from May 2026, plus a documented trespass arrest ending in men's-ward holding. If anything goes wrong at entry, custody is where severity escalates: immigration abuse and federal conversion-style prison policies are documented state conduct, and rule of law is a liability there. Countervailing, the state does not criminalise trans identity itself, no execution pathway exists, and courts repeatedly enjoin or block hostile measures while federal hate-crime and employment protections survive. Majority-hostile polling and division-level gaps (no hate-crime statute) hold the rating down. Net: elevated risk, 0.45.
